fullPassage:
Throughout history, humans and animals have worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped round up sheep, horses and cows helped with farming, and some animals assisted with hunting and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has always been a vital part of human history.
Recent studies, however, reveal there's another aspect to this story. It turns out that wild animals, those that haven't been specifically bred to live with humans, are also willing to form mutual relationships with humans. One outstanding example is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used drones and underwater cameras to observe this unique partnership. When migrating mullets approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins drive them towards the coast, where fishers stand ready to catch them with their nets. The fishers watch the dolphins, looking for them to communicate that they will be making a "deep dive," which lasts about 15 seconds. Fishers then cast their nets just as the dolphins drive the mullets towards the surface.
As a result, the fishers catch much more fish, and the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to escape from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that engage in this fishing are more likely to live longer, by 13 percent. Without this cooperation, dolphins may end up swimming to areas where there aren't many fish, and in doing so, get caught in illegal fishing nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way to catch fish. It's a win-win for both humans and animals, a reminder of how our interactions and relationships with the natural world can be mutually beneficial. This harmony has kept the tradition alive for generations, and it continues to inspire us today.

ch: 야생 돌고래와 어부의 상호 이익적 협력 관계
해양 생태계 보전을 위한 국제적 노력
questions.passage:
Throughout history, humans and animals have worked together in a variety of ways. Dogs helped round up sheep, horses and cows helped with farming, and some animals assisted with hunting and guarding. Raising and breeding animals has always been a vital part of human history.
Recent studies, however, reveal there's another aspect to this story. It turns out that wild animals, those that haven't been specifically bred to live with humans, are also willing to form mutual relationships with humans. One outstanding example is in Laguna, Brazil, where dolphins and fishers have teamed up to catch fish for over 130 years.
A 15-year study conducted by researchers used drones and underwater cameras to observe this unique partnership. When migrating mullets approach the shore in large groups, some dolphins drive them towards the coast, where fishers stand ready to catch them with their nets. The fishers watch the dolphins, looking for them to communicate that they will be making a "deep dive," which lasts about 15 seconds. Fishers then cast their nets just as the dolphins drive the mullets towards the surface.
As a result, the fishers catch much more fish, and the dolphins get to eat mullets trying to escape from the net. Amazingly, dolphins that engage in this fishing are more likely to live longer, by 13 percent. Without this cooperation, dolphins may end up swimming to areas where there aren't many fish, and in doing so, get caught in illegal fishing nests.
The 130-year partnership between the dolphins and the fishers of Laguna is more than just a way to catch fish. It's a win-win for both humans and animals, a reminder of how our interactions and relationships with the natural world can be mutually beneficial. This harmony has kept the tradition alive for generations, and it continues to inspire us today.
questions.stem: 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 야생 돌고래와 어부의 상호 이익적 협력 관계.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 상호 이익적 협력: mutual relationships + win-win + mutually beneficial
❌ ① 어업 기술: 기술 발전이 아닌 자연 협력
❌ ③ 돌고래 훈련: 야생 동물이며 훈련하지 않음
❌ ④ 국제 노력: 라구나 한 지역 사례
det.tip: mutual + win-win + beneficial = 상호 이익 핵심어

questions.stem:
다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

"Even (A)__________ animals can form partnerships with humans that are (B)__________."

det.korean: (A) 야생(wild) 동물도 (B) 상호 이로운(mutually beneficial) 파트너십을 형성할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ wild–mutually beneficial: 야생 동물 + 상호 이익 = 핵심
❌ ① domesticated(가축화된): wild의 반대
❌ ② trained(훈련된): 야생이며 훈련 없음
❌ ④ captive(포획된): 자유 상태
det.tip: wild animals(야생 동물) + mutually beneficial(상호 이로운)

"The dolphin-fisher tradition in Laguna has been passed down through __________.". (1단어)

det.korean: 라구나의 돌고래-어부 전통은 여러 세대(generations)에 걸쳐 전해져 왔다.
det.analysis: 원문 'kept the tradition alive for generations' → generations
det.tip: for generations = 여러 세대에 걸쳐 / passed down through generations = 세대를 통해 전해진
